name: Chang Wen-chang
bio: Chang Wen-chang is a Chinese poet named in Charles Budd’s Chinese Poems (1912). Budd places him in the T’ang dynasty and gives no further note for him.
The poems here are Charles Budd’s versions in Chinese Poems (1912), given under the poet’s name as Budd romanises it.

poems.title: The Old Temple among the Mountains
poems.author: Chang Wen-chang
poems.text:
The temple courts with grasses rank abound,
And birds throng in the forest trees around;
But pilgrims few, though tablets still remain,
Come to the shrine while revolutions reign.

The mice climb through the curtains--full of holes,
And thick dust overspreads the broidered stoles;
The temple pool in gloomy blackness lies
To which the sleeping dragon sometimes hies.
